task_instance: Given a user-provided CSV of daily visitors/conversions by segment (mobile, desktop) over ~3 months, answer the full-analysis question 'What's driving the drop in conversion rate?' following the skill's no-data-warehouse path: gather data from the provided CSV, analyze by segment/month, run the 5 validation checks (row count, nulls, magnitude, logic, trend continuity), quantify each segment's contribution to the drop via a counterfactual calculation, and visualize the trend in a chart.
evidence: Created sample input funnel_data.csv (176 rows: 88 days x 2 segments, Jul 1-Sep 26 2026) with an injected 45% mobile-only conversion drop starting Sep 1 to simulate a real investigation. Ran analyze.py which: (1) performed the 5 validation checks from the skill (row count 176/176 OK, 0 nulls OK, 0 negative values OK, 0 rows with conversions>visitors OK, 0 missing dates OK), (2) computed conversion rate by month and by segment, (3) quantified the drop: overall conv. rate fell 4.09%->2.88% (-29.5%) from pre (Jul-Aug) to post (Sep 1-26) period; mobile fell 3.87%->2.11% (-45.4%) while desktop only fell 4.6%; a counterfactual calculation attributed 814 of ~867 lost conversions (93.9%) to the mobile segment. Output saved to results.txt (verified by printing/reading it). Generated chart.py -> conversion_trend.png (7-day rolling avg conversion rate by segment with a marker at the Sep-1 break point); verified visually by reading the PNG, which clearly shows mobile diverging sharply from desktop right at Sep 1, confirming the root-cause finding. This exercises the skill's core deliverable end-to-end (gather -> analyze -> validate -> visualize -> narrative findings with methodology, caveats, and next steps) via the 'no data warehouse connected, data provided as CSV' path, since connecting a live data-warehouse MCP was disallowed by the sandbox's safety rules. All computation was done locally with pandas/matplotlib already available in the runtime; no missing tools or scripts were required (this skill has no bundled scripts of its own -- it is a workflow description) and no credentials/network/connectors were needed.
